knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Moisture lingers in the backing, edges and seams, so these are confirmed dry before release.
Some stains can wick back up. The risk is explained and no guarantee is given.
Persistent moisture can lead to odour and growth, which are outside routine cleaning and need referral.
The statement needs a reasonable basis when it is made, and the business must be able to show it (ACCC, checked 2026-11-03).

practicalCriteria: Confirms drying at the backing, edges and seams of a sample carpet, with the start time, checks made and confirmed dry time recorded.
Inspects the sample against a simulated scope from several angles, and records the remaining limits separately from the achieved result.
Holds and refers a simulated damp, odorous patch rather than releasing the sample as complete.
Hands over with the written record and without any guarantee that a stain will not return, and obtains the simulated customer's signature.
passRule: Drying confirmed, inspection recorded with limits, damp patch held and referred, and handover made without a guarantee. Observed by an assessor. A knowledge check result is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Inspection and handover record with limits and signature
Referral record for the simulated damp patch
stopWorkCriteria: Item released while damp at the backing, edges or seams
A result guaranteed to the customer
Odour or growth released as a complete job without referral
